ulmic: Pertaining to ulmin; designating an acid obtained from ulmin.
ultion: The act of taking vengeance; revenge. (old) Sir T. Browne.
ulva: A genus of thin papery bright green seaweeds including the kinds called sea lettuce.
ultraviolet: Lying outside the visible spectrum at its violet end; -- said of rays more refrangible than the extreme violet rays of the spectrum.
ultroneous: Spontaneous; voluntary. (old) Jer. Taylor. -- Ul*tro"ne*ous*ly, adv. (old) -- Ul*tro"ne*ous*ness, n. (old)
ullmannite: A brittle mineral of a steel-gray color and metallic luster, containing antimony, arsenic, sulphur, and nickel.
ulmus: A genus of trees including the elm.
ulotrichous: Having woolly or crispy hair; -- opposed to leiotrichous.
ultimatum: A final proposition, concession, or condition; especially, the final propositions, conditions, or terms, offered by either of the parties in a diplomatic negotiation; the most favorable terms a negotiator can offer, the rejection of which usually puts an end to the hesitation.
ulna: 1. (Anat.) The postaxial bone of the forearm, or branchium, corresponding to the fibula of the hind limb. See Radius. 2. (O. Eng. Law) An ell; also, a yard. Burrill.
ultimately: As a final consequence; at last; in the end; as, afflictions often tend to correct immoral habits, and ultimately prove blessings.
ultramontanism: The principles of those within the Roman Catholic Church who maintain extreme views favoring the pope's supremacy; -- so used by those living north of the Alps in reference to the Italians; -- rarely used in an opposite sense, as referring to the views of those living north of the Alps and opposed to the papal claims. Cf. Gallicanism.
ultrared: Situated beyond or below the red rays; as, the ultrated rays of the spectrum, which are less refrangible than the red.
ule: A Mexican and Central American tree (Castilloa elastica and C. Markhamiana) related to the breadfruit tree. Its milky juice contains caoutchouc. Called also ule tree.
ultravires: Beyond power; transcending authority; -- a phrase used frequently in relation to acts or enactments by corporations in excess of their chartered or statutory rights.
ulnare: One of the bones or cartilages of the carpus, which articulates with the ulna and corresponds to the cuneiform in man.
ultimation: State of being ultimate; that which is ultimate, or final; ultimatum. Swift.
ultima: Most remote; furthest; final; last. Ultima ratio Etym: [L.], the last reason or argument; the last resort. -- Ultima Thule. [L.] See Thule.
ultraism: The principles of those who advocate extreme measures, as radical reform, and the like. Dr. H. More.
ultimate: 1. Farthest; most remote in space or time; extreme; last; final. My harbor, and my ultimate repose. Milton. Many actions apt to procure fame are not conductive to this our ultimate happiness. | 1. To come or bring to an end; to eventuate; to end. 2. To come or bring into use or practice.
ulotrichi: The division of mankind which embraces the races having woolly or crispy hair. Cf. Leiotrichi.
ululate: To howl, as a dog or a wolf; to wail; as, ululating jackals. Sir T. Herbert.
ulexite: A mineral occurring in white rounded crystalline masses. It is a hydrous borate of lime and soda.
ullet: A European owl (Syrnium aluco) of a tawny color; -- called also uluia.
ultimo: In the month immediately preceding the present; as, on the 1st ultimo; -- usually abbreviated to ult. Cf. Proximo.
ulema: A college or corporation in Turkey composed of the hierarchy, namely, the imams, or ministers of religion, the muftis, or doctors of law, and the cadis, or administrators of justice.
ultra: A prefix from the Latin ultra beyond (see Ulterior), having in composition the signification beyond, on the other side, chiefly when joined with words expressing relations of place; as, ultramarine, ultramontane, ultramundane, ultratropical, etc. In other relations it has the sense of excessively, exceedingly, beyond what is common, natural, right, or proper;
ultramundane: Being beyond the world, or beyond the limits of our system. Boyle.
ulotrichan: Of or pertaining to the Ulotrichi. -- n. One of the Ulotrichi.
ultramarine: Situated or being beyond the sea. Burke. | A blue pigment formerly obtained by powdering lapis lazuli, but now produced in large quantities by fusing together silica, alumina, soda, and sulphur, thus forming a glass, colored blue by the…
ulula: A genus of owls including the great gray owl (Ulula cinerea) of Arctic America, and other similar species. See Illust. of Owl.
ulster: A long, loose overcoat, worn by men and women, originally made of frieze from Ulster, Ireland.
ultratropical: Situated beyond, or outside of, the tropics; extratropical; also, having an excessively tropical temperature; warmer than the tropics.
uliginous: Muddy; oozy; slimy; also, growing in muddy places. Woodward.
ulcerate: To be formed into an ulcer; to become ulcerous. | To affect with, or as with, an ulcer or ulcers. Harvey.
ulnar: Of or pertaining to the ulna, or the elbow; as, the ulnar nerve.
ululation: A howling, as of a dog or wolf; a wailing. He may fright others with his ululation. Wither.
ulcerative: Of or pertaining to ulcers; as, an ulcerative process.
ultrazodiacal: Outside the zodiac; being in that part of the heavens that is more than eight degrees from the ecliptic; as, ultrazodiacal planets, that is, those planets which in part of their orbits go beyond the zodiac.
ulmin: A brown amorphous substance found in decaying vegetation. Cf. Humin. [Formerly written ulmine.]
ulcerous: 1. Having the nature or character of an ulcer; discharging purulent or other matter. R. Browning. 2. Affected with an ulcer or ulcers; ulcerated. It will but skin and film the ulcerous place. Shak. -- Ul"cer*ous*ly, adv. -- Ul"cer*ous*ness, n.
ultragaseous: Having the properties exhibited by gases under very low pressures (one millionth of an atmosphere or less). Matter under this condition, which has been termed the fourth state of matter, is sometimes called radiant matter.
ularburong: A large East Indian nocturnal tree snake (Dipsas dendrophila). It is not venomous.
ulmaceous: Of or pertaining to a suborder of urticaceous plants, of which the elm is the type.
ultimity: The last stage or consequence; finality. (old) Bacon.
ullage: The amount which a vessel, as a cask, of liquor lacks of being full; wantage; deficiency.
ulceration: The process of forming an ulcer, or of becoming ulcerous; the state of being ulcerated; also, an ulcer.
ulonata: A division of insects nearly equivalent to the true Orthoptera.
ultraist: One who pushes a principle or measure to extremes; an extremist; a radical; an ultra.
uliginose: Muddy; oozy; slimy; also, growing in muddy places. Woodward.
ulcerated: Affected with, or as with, an ulcer or ulcers; as, an ulcerated sore throat.
ulcer: 1. (Med.) A solution of continuity in any of the soft parts of the body, discharging purulent matter, found on a surface, especially one of the natural surfaces of the body, and originating generally in a constitutional disorder; a sore discharging pus. It is distinguished from an abscess, which has its beginning, at least, in the depth of the tissues. 2.
ultramontane: Being beyond the mountains; specifically, being beyond the Alps, in respect to the one who speaks. Note: This term was first applied, somewhat contemptuously, by the Italians, to the nations north of… | 1. One who resides beyond the mountains, especially beyond the Alps; a foreigner. 2. One who maintains extreme views favoring the pope's supremacy. See Ultramontanism.
ulterior: 1. Situated beyond, or on the farther side; thither; -- correlative with hither. 2. Further; remoter; more distant; succeeding; as, ulterior demands or propositions; ulterior views; | Ulterior side or part. Coleridge.
